quality_notes.issue: parse_consolidated_pdf.py's block-opening detection (blocks_from) only starts a new block at an enumerator when the accumulated text so far already ends in ';:.-–—' or 'or'/'and' -- the signal it uses to tell a genuine new list item from a cross-reference that happens to land beside a bracketed letter mid-sentence. The FIRST item after an intro clause that ends in ordinary words ('...the Government Agent shall cause to be prepared (a) a scheme...') doesn't satisfy that, so it stays fused into the section/subsection's own text; whichever item comes next (here, (b)) DOES split correctly, because by then the accumulated text ends in a semicolon from the fused-in first item. The same shape recurs with the SECOND item missing in section 2's 'land' definition (paragraph (a)'s raw_text swallows (b)'s content instead of the reverse) -- it is not specific to which letter, only to whichever item follows non-punctuated lead-in text. A general fix (giving parse_consolidated_pdf.py an equivalent of build_canonical_statutes.py's split_enumerated, which scans a whole accumulated text for enumerator tokens rather than relying on line-by-line continuity signals) is real future work, not attempted here given two other general fixes in this same area regressed already-finalized statutes earlier in this session.
